claims.claim: 800 req/s at peak is a small load for a service doing one indexed lookup; well within one Spring Boot pod's capacity, a few pods per data centre give headroom
claims.measured: Single-row Postgres query on 1 CPU: java-spring 7,668 req/s (p99 77.87 ms); java-spring-vt 12,731 req/s (p99 12.39 ms)
claims.why: One CPU of Spring Boot handled roughly 10–16 times the 800 req/s peak in the single-query DB test, so one pod covering it is in line with the measurements.

claims.claim: The 150 ms p99 budget isn't set by the language
claims.measured: Single-query p99 at 64 connections, fully loaded: java-spring 77.87 ms, java-spring-vt 12.39 ms, go-gin 6.00 ms, go-nethttp 7.10 ms; php-laravel 486.58 ms
claims.why: Java and Go both stayed under 150 ms p99 even at saturation, far above 800 req/s, though the claim does not hold for every language (Laravel went over).

claims.claim: Go will use less memory and start faster than Spring Boot
claims.measured: Peak memory in single-query DB test: Go 11–12 MB vs Spring 307–499 MB; start-up: Go 238–293 ms vs Spring 5,939–6,224 ms
claims.why: The measurements point the same way, and by a wide margin.

claims.claim: Spring Boot pods typically need a few hundred MB
claims.measured: Idle 131–134 MB; peak 307–499 MB in the DB tests
claims.why: Measured peak memory under load was 300–500 MB, which matches "a few hundred MB".

claims.claim: The memory difference between Go and Spring Boot is maybe a gigabyte across the fleet
claims.measured: Per-pod peak difference about 295 MB (spring-vt 307 MB vs Go 12 MB) to about 490 MB (spring 499 MB vs Go 11 MB)
claims.why: The total depends on a pod count the answer never fixes; with "a few pods" in each of several data centres it could be 2–3 GB, not 1.

claims.claim: Java 21 virtual threads let blocking JDBC calls scale without a reactive rewrite
claims.measured: Single query: vt 12,731 req/s, p99 12.39 ms vs platform threads 7,668 req/s, p99 77.87 ms; 20 queries: 1,699 vs 1,254 req/s
claims.why: Virtual threads gave higher throughput and much lower p99 on the blocking-DB tests.

claims.claim: Go is technically fine but buys little (in performance) for this service
claims.measured: Single query: go-gin 22,138 req/s, p99 6.00 ms vs spring-vt 12,731 req/s, p99 12.39 ms; memory 12 MB vs 307 MB
claims.why: Go's throughput lead is under 2x and both run far above 800 req/s within the latency budget; the memory gap is large, but the answer admits that separately.

claims.claim: Quarkus or Micronaut give faster start-up and lower memory than Spring Boot
claims.why: Neither Quarkus nor Micronaut was measured.
